The LLM can pick a registered sub-agent or tool, and dynamic workflow nodes can choose among pre-built nodes at runtime, but sub-agent system prompts, tools and models are fixed in Go code at construction. Remote A2A agents can be resolved from the Cloud Agent Registry at startup.

Members are pre-registered or produced by a callable factory / TeamFactory under host control. StudioTools lets an agent create or edit agent/team components at runtime, but writes are DRAFTs that serve nothing until published; there is no ad-hoc 'spawn a sub-agent with this prompt' primitive.
Each agent is a Rust type with #[agent(...)] macro. No markdown configs, no inline per-call configs, no runtime synthesis.

AgentDefinition is a dataclass the Python harness can build per-request per-tenant (no requirement that the dict be static at boot). The parent LLM itself cannot generate a new AgentDefinition mid-run, but host-side dynamic registration is supported.

Corrected from 'static at session start': Options.agents can be built per request, and the parent LLM can choose the per-call model, background and isolation, and write Workflow scripts that compose registered agents. It still cannot define a new agent type (system prompt + tools); subagent_type must name a registered agent. Now level with the Python SDK (3); previously 1.
Sub-agents must be statically registered (in code, YAML, or fetched from AMP repository at boot). DelegateWorkTool only lets the LLM pick among pre-registered coworkers.

Not supported. The deep task tool lets the LLM pick a subagent_type from a fixed registry and supply a free-text description; sub-agents are Go structs built before the run (TurnLoop PrepareAgent can vary the set per turn, in host code).

Not provided. The parent LLM chooses which registered sub-agent to call and writes the task text, but cannot define a new sub-agent's prompt or tools at runtime unless you write a generic tool that forwards a free-form prompt to Generate.
parent.add_node(name, agent) is build-time. No inline-per-call config. Closest is dynamic-model selection inside an existing sub-agent (chat_agent_executor.py:325-356).
Not first-class. You can build a FunctionAgent dynamically inside a tool, but there's no markdown-loader analogue to Claude's Task tool.

agents can be a DynamicArgument returning the map per request, enabling per-tenant persona fan-out. The LLM picks an existing agent-<name> tool; it can pass additional instructions/maxSteps/threadId/resourceId merged onto the sub-agent's defaults.
Parent LLM cannot create a new sub-agent with a custom system prompt at runtime. Sub-agents must be registered ahead of time. Workaround: BYO custom tool constructing Agent from a dict.

Local sub-agents are static Python Agent objects. The experimental hosted multi-agent model (0.18.2+) lets the root model decide which sub-agents to spawn and what to tell them, but they inherit the same model and toolset and run only on OpenAI's service. Small primitive; previously 0.

SDK agents are statically declared TypeScript. The experimental OpenAI-hosted Multi-agent model lets the hosted root decide which sub-agents to spawn and what to tell them, but every hosted agent shares the same model and tool definitions and it is OpenAI-only. Small primitive, capped as experimental; previously 0.

Within SubAgents the parent picks which registered agent and which model key from a menu; DynamicWorkflow lets the model write the orchestration (fan-out, chaining, voting) as sandboxed code over a fixed catalog and reveal() sub-agents mid-run; CapabilityCreation writes capability code that activates on the next run. Fully ad-hoc sub-agent specs from the LLM remain BYO (Agent.from_spec). Harness is 0.x. Previously 1.
Sub-agents are statically registered Rust structs built via AgentBuilder. The parent LLM cannot dynamically generate a sub-agent's preamble or toolset.

In the SDK this is still not provided, but the first-party Beta harness subagent/make_subagent exposes instructions, tools, MCP servers, model and context as Fixed/Inherit/Open/Choice, so the model can write an ad-hoc role prompt, narrow tools (never widen) and pick a model. Scored on that capability and capped at 4 for Beta. Previously 1 (use_agent BYO).

The SDK still builds configs in code, but harness-ts's subagent tool can expose Open(...) parameters such as free-form instructions to the parent model, with the child unable to gain tools the parent lacked. The report read only the design header, not the default configuration or maturity, so scored below the Python harness (4). Previously 0.
No native support. A meta-tool can instantiate a ToolLoopAgent from LLM-provided arguments, but the SDK has no opinion or telemetry/streaming integration for it.

agenttool is strongest: a fresh in-memory session per call, with sub-agent events not stored in the parent session. Single-turn/task tools and graph nodes share the session but are separated by branch (WithUseSubBranch) and, for task mode, IsolationScope; an LlmAgent at a graph node defaults to single-turn and does not see chat history. Isolation is a history filter over shared storage except for agenttool.

Each member call passes a copy of run_context.session_state (team/_default_tools.py:831) so mutations don't bleed back. All members share session_id; knowledge filters fall back to leader's if member has none.

Each agent owns its own BaseAgent with its own memory/tools/context. Parent's memory is not shared; isolation enforced by Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn MemoryProvider>>> ownership and no shared mutable state at the framework level.

Each sub-agent has its own transcript JSONL under subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl. Parent sees only final summary; sub-agent's system prompt is its own (AgentDefinition.prompt) and parent's context is not inherited.

Sub-agent starts fresh: only its own system prompt, optional initialPrompt, and its own tool catalog. Parent only gets the final result (or with forwardSubagentText:true, the intermediate text). Separate session subpath on disk.

Each Agent has its own executor.messages list — Crew agents do not share message history unless explicitly wired via context in Task.execute_sync. Delegated coworker receives only the task+context strings.

agentTool runs a fresh runner over the inner agent with a shared parent session (k-v values); input is the tool argument or full history with WithFullChatHistoryAsInput. Parallel branches fork runContext (shared Values, isolated events until commit); transfer agents inherit the same context; skill fork modes choose fresh or replayed context. ClearRunCtx gives explicit isolation.

Fresh by default: server-managed sub-agents receive only the task message, client-managed ones the last HistoryLength user/model text messages. The Go context.Context/ActionContext is shared, so tenant identity carries through, and each server-managed sub-agent keeps its own session.

Not enforced; depends on state schema design. Same state_schema means the subgraph sees the parent's full messages; its own schema isolates except for explicit channel mapping, and Command(graph=Command.PARENT) lets a subgraph write to parent state.
Each sub-agent invocation via .run() gets its own Context by default — fresh memory, fresh state. Can opt-in to ctx=parent_ctx for sharing.

The sub-agent gets a sanitized copy of parent messages (parent tool parts stripped; delegation.messageFilter can narrow further) and its own RequestContext without MastraMemory or thread/resource keys. Caveat: an LLM-supplied resourceId on the agent-* tool becomes the sub-agent's memory scope (${resourceId}-${agentName}), so hosts should scope sub-agent memory explicitly.

as_tool(propagate_session=False) gives a private session by default; True forwards a copy of parent state minus approval and budget keys. BackgroundAgentsProvider runs each task in its own sub-session. as_tool forwards function_invocation_kwargs to the child, background agents do not.

as_tool builds a fresh ToolContext for the child: same context object and shared usage, but approvals are not shared with the parent (correction: the May report said otherwise). The child sees only the input the parent generated, not its history. Handoffs are the opposite (full history, optional HandoffInputFilter, which is not a redaction mechanism).

Nested asTool runs share the parent's RunContext.context, approvals and usage (runContext _cloneSharedState) but start from the tool input, not the parent's message history. Handoffs pass history, filterable with HandoffInputFilter (rejected on main when combined with server-managed conversation state).

Fresh run with its own message history; the child never sees the parent conversation. Deps are forwarded (same AgentDepsT), usage is shared by default (forward_usage=False to separate), the parent's tools are not passed, and depth is capped (max_depth, default 3). Applies to core delegation and the harness SubAgents.

History is isolated: the sub-agent starts a fresh run with only args.prompt. Identity is deliberately not isolated: the parent's ToolContext is inherited via context.for_dispatch(), so tenant identity flows down; hooks, memory and model come from the sub-agent's own configuration.

as_tool(preserve_context=False) (default) snapshots the child's initial state and resets before every call; Graph/Swarm nodes follow the same pattern. The child never sees the parent's agent.messages; only the input string crosses. Incompatible with a child session_manager.

AgentAsTool.preserveContext defaults to false (sub-agent reloads initial snapshot before each call). Sub-agent does not see parent's agent.messages either way; only the input string crosses the boundary.
Each child ToolLoopAgent.generate() starts with whatever messages you give it. No automatic parent-context inheritance, no automatic redaction. Fully BYO behaviour.

Depends on mechanism: agenttool returns the last text as {result: text} (structured if OutputSchema is set, linked by function call ID, artifacts forwarded); single-turn/task tools return {result: ...} typed from Input/OutputSchema; graph nodes emit typed Output values and a JoinNode aggregates map[node]output. Transfer and legacy workflow agents stream child events straight into the parent iterator.

Each member run returns a RunOutput/TeamRunOutput whose content becomes the delegation tool result in the leader's loop. TeamMode controls handling (coordinate synthesises, route returns directly, broadcast, tasks). All member runs are collected on TeamRunOutput.member_responses and stored with parent_run_id.

Sub-agent output reaches the parent only via Event::TaskComplete{sub_id, actor_name, result} on the runtime's event stream. No tool_use_id linkage because sub-agents are not modelled as tool calls. Parent must filter/assemble manually.

The parent LLM receives a single result string as a ToolResultBlock linked by tool_use_id. The harness additionally gets Task*Message lifecycle with usage, nested tool blocks carrying parent_tool_use_id, and with forward_subagent_text=True the sub-agent's text and thinking; resumed transcripts carry parent_tool_use_id/parent_agent_id.

The result returns as a tool_result linked by tool_use_id with a published AgentToolCompletedOutput shape (agentId, content, resolvedModel, totalTokens, durationMs, usage, toolStats, status completed/async_launched). forwardSubagentText:true forwards nested assistant text with parent_tool_use_id; background agents deliver via task_notification.

Crew delegation returns one string as the tool result. Flow methods return Python values to downstream listeners. Conversational Flows append agent results to a private agent thread and optionally to the public transcript (visible_agent_outputs). No parent tool-use linkage outside A2A events.

agentTool returns the last assistant message content as a single string, linked by tool_call_id; inner interrupts propagate as CompositeInterrupt. ToolsConfig.EmitInternalEvents streams sub-agent events to the parent iterator (UI-only, not in the parent session), fixed for the agentic path in v0.9. Skill fork mode can shape the result via FormatForkResult.

The experimental delegate tool returns a structured result (response, artifacts, taskId, status, name) linked by the tool request Ref, and artifacts are merged into the parent session under namespaced names. Sub-agent failures and interrupts are folded into the result text rather than propagated. Capped at 4 as experimental; previously 3 (single ToolResponse.Output).

Subgraph as node: the final state becomes the node's writes and parent channel reducers merge them. Subgraph as tool: ToolMessage.content string linked by tool_call_id; in v3 streaming the child's lifecycle events also carry cause.tool_call_id. Flexible via state design.

agents-as-tools: awaits .run() and returns the result string linked via tool_id. AgentWorkflow handoff switches current_agent_name and continues; the final result is an AgentOutput, and since 0.14.24 each active agent's own structured-output config populates structured_response.

The synthesized agent-<name> tool returns structured {text, subAgentThreadId, subAgentResourceId, subAgentToolResults, ref?}, linked by toolCallId. By default toModelOutput exposes only text to the supervisor (includeSubAgentToolResultsInModelContext opts in); enableResultReferences adds refs reusable via contextFromRefs; nested chunks stream via fullStream in network mode.

as_tool: the parent receives a string function_result linked by call_id; child approval requests are not propagated. BackgroundAgentsProvider: results pulled via get_task_results with task state persisted in the session. Orchestrations standardise terminal output as AgentResponse plus workflow events.

as_tool returns the nested agent's final_output as the tool result (custom_output_extractor can rewrite), linked by call_id; on_stream re-emits nested events as AgentToolStreamEvent. Handoffs continue the same RunResult. In experimental hosted multi-agent only the root final answer reaches RunResult; sub-agent messages are raw events.

asTool: the nested agent's final output becomes the function tool result (string by default, customOutputExtractor overrides), linked by callId; the full nested RunResult is on FunctionToolResult.agentRunResult. Handoff: the new agent's final output. Hosted Multi-agent: only the root answer becomes finalOutput.

delegate_task returns str(result.output) as a normal tool result linked by tool_call_id, with soft outcomes (timeout, budget, max_calls) returned as steering text, model errors as ModelRetry and crashes contained on request (contain_errors). DelegationEndEvent also carries output, usage and outcome. Output is still a string and core delegation is BYO; capped at 4 for the 0.x harness. Previously 3.

The parent receives ToolOutput::text(response.output), the sub-agent's final text, as a normal tool result bound to the parent's CallId; failures become ToolExecutionError. No sub-agent event streaming and no structured output by default.

_AgentAsTool.stream yields AgentAsToolStreamEvent per child event, then a ToolResultEvent with [{text}] or [{json: structured_output}], linked by tool_use_id; a paused child yields ToolInterruptEvent. With delegate=True the child's content blocks become the parent's final answer.

asTool returns a ToolResultBlock with the sub-agent's structured output as a JsonBlock or a TextBlock; thrown errors and cancelled children become error results. Linked via toolUseId. Graph/Swarm aggregate into MultiAgentResult streamed as MultiAgentStreamEvents.

Still whatever the tool returns, but the documented pattern (async-generator tool + readUIMessageStream) streams the child's growing UIMessage as preliminary tool outputs linked to the parent toolCallId, and toModelOutput decides what the parent model sees. All of it is BYO wiring. Corrected: the May report understated this documented pattern; previously 2.

No dedicated sub-agent started/completed event; lifecycle is inferred from Author, Branch, IsolationScope and NodeInfo.Path changes on events forwarded into the parent iterator. Telemetry has explicit spans (invoke_agent per agent, invoke_node per workflow node, per-item spans for parallel workers).

Corrected: there are no MemberDelegationStarted/Completed events. Member events are forwarded into the team stream (stream_member_events, default on) with parent_run_id on each frame, and TeamToolCallStarted/Completed bracket each delegation. Comparable to openai-agents' AgentToolStreamEvent, so lowered from 5 (correction). Paused member runs persist for HITL resume.

The parent sees TaskStarted, TurnStarted/Completed, ToolCallRequested/Completed and TaskComplete from child agents via the runtime's shared broadcast channel; filter by actor_id/actor_name/sub_id. v0.4.0 guarantees a terminal TaskComplete or TaskError for actor streaming runs, so a silently failed child no longer hangs the parent.

Dedicated TaskStarted/Progress/Notification/Updated messages carry task_id, description, usage and status (with TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES). Combined with SubagentStart/SubagentStop hooks and optional forward_subagent_text, the parent observes sub-agent lifecycle in flight. A killed task may only report status through TaskUpdatedMessage.

SubagentStart/Stop and TaskCreated/TaskCompleted hooks, plus stream messages task_started (is_backgrounded, spawn_depth), task_progress (summaries with agentProgressSummaries), task_updated, task_notification, background_tasks_changed and tool_progress heartbeats with subagent_retry.
AgentExecutionStartedEvent/Completed/Error fire per agent execution. A2A delegation has ~30 events (A2ADelegationStartedEvent, A2AStreamingChunkEvent). Solid coverage.

callbacks.Handler.OnStart/OnEnd fire per agent boundary (RunInfo.Component=ComponentOfAgent; Type distinguishes ChatModel/Sequential/Parallel/Loop/Supervisor). Per-message sub-agent events are not in the parent iterator by default; opt in via ToolsConfig.EmitInternalEvents.

Not streamed to the parent: runSubAgent folds the output and the parent stream shows only the delegation tool call and result. Lifecycle is visible through nested trace spans (Dev UI) and, for background tasks, snapshot status (pending/aborting/completed/failed/aborted/expired) via the polling tools; polling and spans are not events, so the score stays at 2 despite the new tooling.

note: v3 lifecycle channel with tool_call cause
details: v1/v2 stream_mode='tasks' frames are joined by the v3 protocol: a lifecycle channel emits started/completed/failed/interrupted/drained per nested run with graph_name, trigger_call_id and cause.tool_call_id, in-process and over SSE/WebSocket. The SDK exposes thread.subgraphs/subagents handles with their own message and tool-call projections. Dedicated, parent-linked events put this level with the other 5s; previously 4.
On handoff, AgentInput/AgentOutput/AgentStream events are emitted tagged with the new current_agent_name. Parent stream sees each sub-agent's tokens.

DelegationConfig hooks onDelegationStart/onDelegationComplete (with bail to cancel siblings, hookErrorStrategy) and messageFilter. The parent stream sees tool-call/tool-result for each agent-* call; network mode streams nested agent-execution-* chunks.

as_tool: stream_callback receives the child's released updates if set, otherwise only the final result. BackgroundAgentsProvider: status via get_all_tasks, a pull API not a stream. Orchestrations emit group_chat, handoff_sent, magentic_orchestrator and executor_* workflow events.

as_tool(on_stream=callback) receives AgentToolStreamEvent for every inner event with the nested agent and tool_call reference (queue bounded, default 1024). Handoffs surface AgentUpdatedStreamEvent and handoff_requested/occured. Hosted sub-agent lifecycle is only in raw beta events.

Agent.asTool({ onStream }) receives every RunStreamEvent from the nested run plus the triggering toolCall; the pending queue is bounded (default 1024, unreleased on main). Handoffs emit handoff_requested/handoff_occurred and RunAgentUpdatedStreamEvent.

The first-party harness emits DelegationStartEvent/DelegationEndEvent capability events (agent_name, task, model, outcome ok/timeout/budget/failed/contained, output, usage, duration) paired by tool_call_id; event_stream_handler forwards nested model streaming and child runs get nested OTel spans. Capped at 4 for the 0.x harness. Core delegation alone remains BYO; previously 1.

Not provided: no sub-agent started/progress/completed events. The parent sees on_dispatch/on_outcome for the tool call, and the sub-agent's invoke_agent span nests under the parent's execute_tool span when tracing is on.

AgentAsToolStreamEvent forwards each child event to parent stream. Dedicated MultiAgent events for Graph/Swarm: MultiAgentNodeStartEvent, MultiAgentNodeStopEvent, MultiAgentHandoffEvent, MultiAgentNodeStreamEvent, etc.

Parent stream sees ToolStreamUpdateEvent carrying sub-agent's AgentStreamEvent (rewrapped at agent-as-tool.ts:171-175). Graph/Swarm have dedicated events: BeforeNodeCallEvent, AfterNodeCallEvent, NodeResultEvent, MultiAgentHandoffEvent.

note: preliminary tool outputs only; harness progress
details: No dedicated sub-agent event category in ai. Progress reaches the parent only as preliminary tool outputs (documented streaming pattern) or writer.merge; the Claude Code harness adds forwardSubagentText and agentProgressSummaries stream parts. Small primitive, mostly BYO; previously 0.
Every llmagent.Config has its own Model, so a Gemini Pro coordinator with Flash or other-provider workers is a configuration choice; a model registry resolves models by name.
Each member is a full Agent with its own model, fallback_config and reasoning_model; supervisor-Sonnet with worker-Haiku is two Agent(model=...) values.

Every AgentBuilder takes its own Arc<dyn LLMProvider>, so a Sonnet supervisor and Haiku workers wire naturally on the same runtime; each llm can be a PipelineBuilder chain with its own retry/fallback. No built-in per-task router.

AgentDefinition.model accepts an alias (sonnet/opus/haiku/inherit) or a full id, and AgentDefinition.effort sets per-agent reasoning effort. Sonnet supervisor with Haiku workers is the canonical pattern; per-model spend shows in ResultMessage.model_usage.

Three levels: AgentDefinition.model (alias, full id or 'inherit'), a per-call AgentInput.model chosen by the parent model that overrides the definition, and AgentOutput.resolvedModel reporting the model actually used. Haiku workers under an Opus parent is the cost-control pattern.

Each Agent has its own llm; Crew also has manager_llm, planning_llm and chat_llm. New llm_overlay (1.15.22) remaps models by agent role or model string per request via a ContextVar, without editing agent definitions.
Each ChatModelAgentConfig.Model is independent, with per-agent ModelRetryConfig/ModelFailoverConfig in v0.9; skills can pin a model per skill via ModelHub.
Each sub-agent is its own agent with its own model in its prompt or .prompt frontmatter, independent of the orchestrator's model; the same holds for hand-written agents-as-tools.
Each subgraph (sub-agent) is built with its own model argument, and can take a model callable (state, runtime) to pick per turn.
Each agent has its own llm field (also in AgentWorkflow), so orchestrator-on-Sonnet with Haiku workers is a matter of passing different llm objects; same for agents-as-tools.

Every sub-agent declares its own model (static, per-request function, or fallback list). AgentController.resolveSubagentModel (1.73.0-alpha.0, unreleased at analysis time) resolves tenant credentials per run; request-scoped parent model overrides do not cascade to sub-agents.
Each sub-agent is an Agent with its own client and default_options. .NET can also switch model per session with RoutePersistingRoutingChatClient.

Each Agent has its own model, so a supervisor can dispatch to a worker on another model (including litellm) via as_tool or handoff; as_tool(run_config=...) overrides the nested run, and RunConfig.model forces one model for all agents. Hosted multi-agent sub-agents use the root model.

Each Agent pins its own model; Agent.asTool({ runConfig: { model } }) overrides the nested run. On main, an explicit child Model object no longer inherits parent transport overrides. Hosted Multi-agent cannot mix models.

Each Agent has its own model. The harness SubAgents adds a model menu (models={'fast':..., 'deep':...}) so the parent picks per delegation, and agent_overrides for disk agents with a thinking-effort floor.
Each sub-agent is a separate Agent built with its own model; a sub-agent can also register alternative models with model_route and switch via on_model_select.

Each child Agent (as_tool, Graph or Swarm node) carries its own model or ModelRouter. Harness make_subagent lets the developer pin or offer models per child; aux_model moves side calls to a cheaper model.
Each sub-agent has its own model config. Standard pattern: const supervisor = new Agent({ model: sonnet, tools: [haikuWorker] }).
Trivial BYO: each child ToolLoopAgent takes its own model, and prepareStep can switch per step. For harness runtimes the native sub-agent model is the runtime's choice.

Ships a skill.Source loader interface and a MergedSource for composition, but no skills registry, no publish/promote/retire lifecycle and no governance. New in v2.x: an agentregistry client for Google Cloud Agent Registry (agents, MCP servers, model endpoints become RemoteAgent/MCPToolset), but publishing, versioning and IAM live in the Google service and skills are not a resource type there. Skills stay the only locally managed resource with BYO sources; closest informal versioning is git.

Two real pieces: a Registry of non-serialisable objects (tools, models, DBs, agents, teams) that now has add_* mutation helpers and declared-vs-discovered tool tracking, and Studio components, a DB-backed catalog of agent/team/workflow configs with draft/publish/archive, versions and compare-and-set guards, exposed via /components and StudioTools. Skills are in neither (LocalSkills only). Real but partial and not unified across skills/prompts/tools/agents; grew since May but stays at 3.

No Registry, no SkillSource, no plugin marketplace, no versioning, no publish workflow. Only an MCP TOML config loader (now local or remote servers, plus a McpToolsManager with connect/disconnect/status) exists, which is a loader for one resource type, not a general resource manager.

No registry, no source abstraction, no publishing workflow. The SDK's resource manager is the filesystem layout plus the setting_sources flag (user/project/local) and the SdkPluginConfig type=local plugin entries. options.skills/agents/plugins filter per request.

Filesystem discovery from .claude/skills/, .claude/agents/, .claude/commands/, plus plugins: SdkPluginConfig[] (type 'local' only). Plugin marketplaces (git/npm/URL) exist only at the Claude Code settings tier, not as a programmatic registry API. Query.reloadPlugins(), reloadSkills() and setMcpServers() give mid-session refresh. No registry layer, no tenant scoping, no publishing workflow, so the score stays at 2.

OSS now ships a registry client for skills (skills/registry.py, skills/cache.py, crewai skill create|install|publish|list) on the AMP Skills Repository (stable since 1.15.4), next to the AMP Agent Repository (from_repository=) and tool repository. Refs, version pins, a local cache and a publish CLI make it a real, if vendor-locked, resource manager. Still no unified self-hostable registry across skills/agents/prompts/tools, no per-tenant scope and no lifecycle states, hence 3 and not higher.

Provides pluggable interfaces (skill.Backend, skill.AgentHub, skill.ModelHub) and ships only the filesystem Backend. No platform-level registry — you build a Resource Manager on top of these seams. None are layered, scoped, or versioned by default.

The only registry is the in-process *registry.Registry holding actions (tools, models, prompts, retrievers) for one running process — a runtime concept, not a publishing concept. Skills/prompts are loaded from local filesystem or embed.FS only.

OSS ships only BaseStore (put/get/search/list_namespaces/delete) as a 'resource as a row' abstraction — closest is namespace tuples like ('skills', tenant_id, ...). LangGraph Platform's Assistants API is the actual resource manager but sits behind paid hosting.

No registry, no source abstraction, no skill/resource concept. Tools are loaded from Python imports or via a tool_retriever. LlamaHub is a community directory of LlamaPacks but offers no draft/review/promote workflow.

Skills, agents, prompt blocks, scorers and MCP clients live in versioned storage domains with status draft/published/archived, activeVersionId, authorId and visibility; VersionedSkillSource + CompositeVersionedSkillSource over blob storage give content-hashed refs and local>managed>external priority. Per-call version selectors accept versionId or status. Still no single registry spanning files/Git/storage, no Git/OCI source and no environment promotion, so 4 and not 5.

Ships a SkillsSource abstraction with Aggregating/Filtering/Deduplicating/Caching wrappers plus file, in-memory and (experimental) MCP sources, for both Python and .NET; skills graduated to stable in Python 1.11.0 / .NET 1.13.0 and sources are now context-aware. Loader-level composition works, but there is no platform layer above it: no draft/active/retired lifecycle, publishing workflow, versioning or RBAC.

No registry abstraction. Has LazySkillSource/LocalDirLazySkillSource for filesystem skills, MultiProviderMap for model routing, and references to OpenAI-hosted skills by skill_id+version (hosted shell only; publishing happens on the OpenAI platform, not in the SDK). No skills/agents/prompts registry; agents and sandbox capabilities are constructed at boot.

Per-SandboxAgent manifest.entries supports localDir, localFile, dir, file, and gitRepo({repo, ref}) sources — including a real Git source. But it is per-agent only, no cross-agent registry, no versioning beyond git refs, no marketplace.

No registry or publishing workflow, but several first-party partial pieces exist: Skills libraries and SubAgents(agent_folders=) read through a pluggable WorkspaceBackend, AgentSpec.from_file/Agent.from_spec, Logfire ManagedPrompt (versioned, labelled, targeted prompts) and CapabilityCreation manifests. Each resource type has its own mechanism, none unified. Several pieces live in pydantic-ai-harness 0.x (pre-1.0 first-party package), which would cap credit at 4 anyway; raised from 1 because the refreshed report documents these pieces.

The only registry is the in-process ToolSet / ToolServerHandle (add_tool/remove_tool now synchronous, plus ToolCatalog snapshots and static_tool_defs), kept in process memory. rig_core::providers::registry is a provider/model reference registry, not a resource manager. No skill, sub-agent or prompt resource model.

AgentSkills(skills=[...]) is a thin loader with filesystem paths or HTTPS URLs and a ToolRegistry for tools. No registry abstraction over many skills/sub-agents/tools across teams. Closest to a resource model is the load_tools_from_directory hot-reload from ./tools/.
AgentSkills wraps a Map<string, Skill> with four loader sources (instance/dir/parent-dir/URL). No Registry, no ResourceManager, no versioning, no RBAC, no per-tenant scoping at registration time.

customProvider() and createProviderRegistry() are model registries (string-keyed lookup like registry.languageModel('openai:gpt-5'), now also evaluationModel and file/skill upload helpers). HarnessAgent.skills is a per-agent array, not a registry. No skills, sub-agents, prompts or tools registry.

Filesystem source works over any fs.FS including embed.FS; preload wrappers (WithCompletePreloadSource, WithFrontmatterPreloadSource) cache in memory. New agentregistry client loads agents, MCP servers and model endpoints from Google Cloud Agent Registry, but not skills. Git, OCI, cloud blob, Postgres and HTTP skill sources are BYO via skill.Source. Stays at 2: a vendor registry for non-skill resources was already the level credited to CrewAI's AMP agent repos in the May baseline.

LocalSkills(path) for skills (filesystem only). Knowledge content can live in Postgres via Knowledge(contents_db=...) and sessions/memories/traces/components are DB-backed. Git, OCI, cloud blob, vendor registry, HTTP are BYO.

The only first-party loader is the MCP TOML config (McpConfig::from_file, crates/autoagents-toolkit/src/mcp/config.rs:94), which reads MCP server definitions (local command or remote Streamable HTTP url + headers since v0.4.0). Everything else (filesystem skills, git, S3, Postgres, vendor registry, HTTP) is BYO.

Programmatic sources are local: `setting_sources` and `SdkPluginConfig` type 'local' (types.py:2297, 2343). Remote sources exist at the Claude Code settings tier exactly as in TS: `ClaudeAgentOptions.settings` takes inline JSON or a path loaded into the flag-settings layer (types.py:2105-2116), so `extraKnownMarketplaces` / `enabledPlugins` (GitHub, git with ref/sha, npm, URL, sha256-pinned zip) can be passed inline; the SDK's own resume code already handles these keys (`_internal/session_resume.py:391-392`). Not a programmatic registry API, OCI/S3/DB sources are absent, and Python has no `reload_plugins` or `managedSettings` equivalent. Raised from 2 to match TS.

Programmatic sources are local paths (~/.claude, .claude/, plugins type 'local') and MCP servers. Through the Claude Code settings tier (Options.settings / managedSettings) plugin marketplaces can also load from GitHub/git (ref/sha), npm, URL, sha256-verified zip archives and a custom shell-command fetcher, plus Anthropic/org-hosted marketplaces. Not a programmatic SDK API and aimed at developer machines and admin policy; OCI, S3 and DB resource sources are absent. Raised from 2 because the refreshed report documents these remote sources (some existed at 0.3.143 but were under-reported).

Local filesystem skills, inline SKILL.md strings (1.15.2), agents.yaml and prompt_file, plus the AMP Skills Repository ("@org/name[@version]" refs, downloaded and cached), AMP Agent Repository (from_repository=) and tool repository, all behind AMP credentials. No git, OCI, cloud blob or Postgres source. Raised from 2 because the vendor registry now covers skills as well as agents, with a local cache.

Ships only filesystemBackend via NewBackendFromFilesystem(ctx, &Config{BaseDir}). Git, OCI, cloud blob, Postgres, vendor registry, HTTP all require BYO implementations of skill.Backend. Agent and Model hubs are also BYO.

Skills: SkillPaths []string for local filesystem. Prompts: WithPromptDir(path) and/or WithPromptFS(embed.FS) (the dir is the root inside the FS), plus LoadPromptFromSource to register a prompt from a string you fetched. MCP servers can supply tools, prompts and resources at runtime but with no versioning or scoping. No git, OCI, cloud blob, Postgres, vendor registry or HTTP sources; Postgres works for embeddings only.

OSS supports local filesystem via Python imports and Postgres/SQLite via BaseStore (the closest 'resource as a row' abstraction). LangSmith Deployment's Assistants API is a vendor-managed registry but needs the ELv2 server and a paid plan. The CLI resolves Git dependencies and image URIs at build time only, which is packaging, not runtime loading. No native git, OCI, cloud blob or HTTP source.
Tools are loaded from Python imports or via a custom tool_retriever the user wires in. No first-class concept of 'load a skill from S3/GCS/Git'. Integration packages are versioned PyPI distributions.

Local filesystem for skills, VersionedSkillSource backed by BlobStore (S3/GCS/R2 adapters), Postgres via storage.getStore('agents'/'skills'/'favorites'), Mastra Cloud via deployers/cloud package. Git and HTTP are BYO.

FileSkillsSource, in-memory/inline/class skills and a new experimental MCPSkillsSource (skill-md or ZIP archives, digest-verified, Foundry Toolbox integration) ship in Python and .NET, with Aggregating/Filtering/Deduplicating/Caching wrappers. The MCP source is the only first-party remote source; Git, S3/GCS/Azure Blob, OCI, DB and HTTP are BYO SkillsSource subclasses. Raised from 2 for the remote MCP source, capped by its experimental status and single remote kind.

Skills load from LocalDirLazySkillSource, from_=BaseEntry bulk entries (LocalDir, archive, GitRepo), sandbox mounts (S3/rclone) and OpenAI-hosted skills referenced by skill_id+version (hosted shell only). Git and bucket content materialises inside the sandbox, not the SDK process. No OCI, DB or HTTP loader. Raised from 2 (correction: hosted-skill references and from_= entries were already present at 0.17.2) to match OpenAI Agents JS, which has the same git/sandbox model.

Per manifest.entries supports localDir, localFile, dir/file (inline) and gitRepo({repo, ref, subpath}), cloned into the sandbox session. Cloud object storage is reachable only as sandbox mounts (S3 via Mountpoint, Modal/Blaxel buckets, rclone), not as a resource registry. OCI, Postgres, vendor registry and HTTP are not provided.

AgentSpec.from_file and Skills/SubAgents read from any WorkspaceBackend (local, Modal/E2B/Sprites/SSH, or a custom e.g. S3-backed backend); MCP servers supply tools, prompts and resources; Logfire ManagedPrompt loads versioned prompts (prompts only). Git, OCI, S3/GCS, Postgres and HTTP are BYO. Stays at 2: pluggable backends plus a vendor registry for one resource type match the ADK Go level.

rig::loaders (crates/rig-core/src/loaders/) reads local files, and the experimental rig-ecs assets module loads prompts/tools via Bevy assets, but neither is a resource registry. rig-s3vectors and rig-postgres are vector stores, not resource sources. Git, OCI, cloud blob, vendor registry and HTTP are unsupported.

AgentSkills(skills=['./skills/']) for local filesystem; Skill.from_url('https://...') for arbitrary HTTPS skill loading; load_tools_from_directory=True for tool hot-reload from ./tools/. Git via clone-then-point; OCI, cloud blob, Postgres, vendor registry not provided.
AgentSkills has four sources: instance (programmatic), dir, parent-dir, and HTTPS URL via Skill.fromUrl (naive fetch, 30s timeout, no ETag). Git, OCI, S3/GCS, Postgres, vendor registry not provided.

No resource source loader for skills/sub-agents/prompts. createProviderRegistry and customProvider are model registries; the only skill-related addition is an Anthropic Skills API upload helper (uploadSkill) where storage and lookup stay yours, and HarnessAgent.skills takes an array you build. Filesystem, git, OCI, cloud blob, Postgres and HTTP are all BYO.

NewMergedSource queries sources in order; LoadFrontmatter/LoadInstructions/LoadResource return the first source that succeeds (earlier sources have priority). ListFrontmatters errors on duplicate skill names (ErrDuplicateSkill), so explicit 'tenant overrides global' requires a custom subtract/fallback wrapper.

Skills(loaders=[a, b, c]) loads all three; on name collision the later loader wins with a logged warning (agent_skills.py:44-46). No declarative 'S3 source overrides Git source for tenant X' pattern. The Registry only tracks ambiguous knowledge/learning names and refuses them in strict mode.
No source abstraction means no composition. Each MCP server is independent in the TOML config; no precedence/override semantics across sources.

Layered by setting_sources: user (~/.claude/) -> project (<cwd>/.claude/) -> local (settings.local.json), all three load by default. Plugins add another layer. The CLI defines conflict-resolution internally; the SDK does not expose precedence configuration.

Settings precedence is user < project < local < flag < policy (managed, restrictive-only), documented at sdk.d.ts:7286-7290. For same-named resources project wins over user, and plugin skills are namespaced (plugin:skill) so they do not collide. reloadPlugins() re-scans after changes. No caller-controlled merge order like local > tenant-bucket > global-registry.

Two declared layers: per registry ref, project ./skills/{name} then ~/.crewai/skills cache then AMP download (version-pinned refs only accept a matching copy); across inputs, load_skills() resolves in order and first occurrence wins per name (registry refs keyed org/name). Listing tenant sources before global ones lets them override. No explicit 'tenant overrides global' semantic beyond order, same gap as ADK Go. Raised from 2 because the resolution order is now documented behaviour rather than a de-dupe side effect.

Not provided as a primitive — you implement a layered Backend that merges multiple backends and applies your own priority logic (e.g. tenant wins over global by composing two skill.Backend instances).

Skills: SkillPaths are scanned in order into a map, so a later path with the same directory name overwrites an earlier one (scanSkills). Prompts: WithPromptDir and WithPromptFS combine (dir is the root inside the FS), with extra LoadPromptDir calls adding namespaced prompts. No priority or fallback configuration.

BaseStore.search() takes a namespace tuple; you implement 'tenant > global' override by trying ('skills', tenant_id) first and falling back to ('skills', 'global'). No first-class layered source primitive.
Tools come from Python imports or a user-provided tool_retriever; no source-composition primitive at the framework level.

Explicit priority order local > managed > external (workspace-skills.ts:207). CompositeVersionedSkillSource mounts multiple versioned skill trees into a virtual filesystem with optional fallback to a live filesystem source for actively-edited skills.

AggregatingSkillsSource concatenates sources in order; DeduplicatingSkillsSource keeps the first occurrence on a name clash; FilteringSkillsSource applies a predicate that now also receives a SkillsSourceContext. Priority is by source ordering only: no declarative priority/override (local > tenant > global).
With no source abstraction, no composition primitive exists. All resources are Python objects constructed at boot.
A SandboxAgent has one defaultManifest; merging is cloneManifest + processManifest at capability level. No local > tenant > global cascading across manifests; per-manifest only.

Multiple Skills libraries combine but duplicate names are an error, not an override (docs/harness/skills.md). SubAgents has defined precedence: explicit agents > workspace .agents/ > .claude/, or earlier folders first (docs/harness/subagents.md). Tenant-over-global override is BYO (compute an exclude list). Raised from 0 because a declared precedence order now exists for sub-agents, though not for skills.
With no source abstraction, no composition exists. ToolSet has last-insert-wins by HashMap insertion but that is not a configured composition primitive.

Skills from multiple sources are processed in order and later occurrences overwrite earlier ones with a logged warning on duplicate name (agent_skills.py:485-525). MCP load_servers(prefix_with_server_name=True) namespaces tool names per server. No declared priority order or override semantics.
Sources are processed in order and a duplicate name overwrites the earlier one with a warning (agent-skills.ts:226, :234, :284). No priority, fallback or merge configuration.
No mechanism to stack sources for skills/sub-agents/prompts. You build any priority/override logic yourself.

No version field on Frontmatter. Compatibility is a free-text 500-char string with no enforcement. Versioning is whatever your filesystem/git provides; bake a version suffix into the directory name or use commit SHA.

Components have integer config versions with a current pointer, draft vs published stage, pinned member versions (v2.9.0), archive/restore, and runs can target a version. Skills only carry a descriptive metadata.version; the framework does not pin or roll back skills by version.
No per-skill or per-tool versioning. Cargo handles crate versions but not artifact-level versioning.

Plugins carry a manifest version, and the CLI settings tier lets marketplace entries pin a git ref/sha, archives pin a sha256, and `enabledPlugins` accept version constraints; Python reaches these through the `settings` option (types.py:2105) the same way TS does. Skills and sub-agents on disk have no versioning beyond your VCS, and there is no rollback API: replace files and reconnect (Python has no `reloadPlugins()`). The CLI itself is pinned via `_cli_version.py` (2.1.286). Raised from 0 to match TS; the pins live at the settings tier, not in a programmatic API.

Plugins carry a manifest version (reported in system/init and reload_plugins); settings-tier marketplace entries can pin git ref/sha, archives can pin sha256, and enabledPlugins accepts version constraints. Skills and sub-agents on disk have no versioning beyond your VCS, and there is no rollback API (replace files, then reloadPlugins()/reloadSkills()). Raised from 1: pins are immutable-ref capable but live at the settings tier, not a programmatic API.

AMP Skills Repository refs accept @org/name@1.2.0; versions come from metadata.version at publish time, an unpinned ref resolves to the newest, and rollback means pinning an older version. The local cache records version metadata. No immutability guarantee visible in OSS, no pin API for AMP Agent Repository (dashboard-side versions only), and local skills rely on your VCS. Raised from 1 because pinning and publish-time versions are now in the OSS client.
Skills are mutable files or rows; no semver, no content-hash refs, no rollback. You build versioning in your backend.
Skills, prompts, tools are versioned by your source-control and deployment. No @semver, no content-hash, no immutable ref system in the framework.
OSS has no versioning model. LangGraph Platform's Assistants API ships versioned assistants but is paid hosted only.
Integration packages have their own PyPI semver in CHANGELOG.md, but agent resources (skills, sub-agents, tools) have no versioning — they live in your codebase.

Stored entities have integer version numbers, an activeVersionId pointer and rollback by re-activating an older version. Published skill files are SHA-256 content-addressed blobs under a SkillVersionTree manifest, and per-call selection works via versionId or status ('draft' | 'published'). No semver, but immutable content-hash refs.

No version field beyond SkillFrontmatter.compatibility (free-form text) and string metadata. MCP archive skills are digest-verified on fetch, but there is no semver, pinning, immutable ref or rollback.

Skill.compatibility is an opaque marker the SDK does not enforce. OpenAI-hosted skill references (ShellToolSkillReference) accept a skill_id plus version, which pins a platform-side skill version, but only for the hosted shell and managed on the OpenAI platform. No semver, content-hash or rollback in the SDK. Raised from 0 (correction: hosted skill references existed at 0.17.2).
gitRepo({ ref }) lets you pin a Git ref (branch, tag, or SHA). No semver registry, no content-hash addressing beyond what Git provides, no rollback primitive shipped.

Skills and agents have no versioning beyond your VCS and PyPI. Logfire ManagedPrompt (harness 0.x, pre-1.0) gives vendor-side prompt versions and labels with pinning (label='production') and rollouts, for prompts only. Raised from 0 for the prompt versioning primitive; kept at 2 because it covers one resource type and lives in a vendor service.
No versioning for skills, agents, or tools. ToolSet is mutated at runtime.
Skill metadata.version is a free-form field; the loader does not interpret it. Tools have no versioning at all.
Skills have no version field that the SDK reads. UUIDv7 snapshot IDs are used for session checkpoints, not for skills.
No semver, no content-hash, no immutable refs, no rollback for skills/sub-agents/prompts.

Source.ListFrontmatters(ctx) accepts a context so you can write a TenantAwareSource that dispatches per-tenant. Composition works via per-tenant Source + MergedSource(globalSrc, tenantSrc). No first-party TenantAwareSource and no publish-time tenant/scope field on Frontmatter — both layers are BYO.

v3.0.0 per-user isolation (user_isolation=True) covers Studio components: unowned components are shared, owned drafts are visible only to their owner (may_read_draft_configs), and JWT scopes gate /components. That gives a partial registry-side scope with runtime enforcement for components, but not for skills or tools, and there is still no tenant_id or 'publish for tenant X' scope (open issue #9831). Per-tenant skill catalogs need an AgentFactory keyed on a trusted JWT claim. Raised from 1.
No registry-side or runtime scoping primitive.

No registry-side scoping. Runtime per-tenant scoping means materializing tenants/<tid>/.claude/skills/ and setting options.cwd + setting_sources=['project']. options.skills is explicitly a 'context filter, not a sandbox' (types.py:2325-2329): files remain reachable via Read/Bash, so it is not safe for tenant isolation of sensitive logic.

No publish-time scoping and no tenantId -> skills mapping API. Runtime scoping is physical and per session: per-tenant cwd, plugin directory and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with settingSources: [], plus Options.skills/tools/agents/mcpServers filters and managedSettings policy per query(). Same gap as the Python SDK.

Skills published to the AMP Skills Repository are always org-scoped (is_public=False, no public visibility), and access depends on the org credentials supplied; AMP RBAC is org/role granularity. Within an org there is no per-tenant or per-user scope at publish time and no runtime filter other than which refs/paths you pass at Agent construction. Raised from 1 for registry-side org scoping; per-tenant catalogs remain one-org-per-tenant or per-tenant directories.

The Backend interface gets ctx context.Context on every List/Get so you can filter by tenant from ctx (filterByTenantPolicy). No first-class skill-scope field in FrontMatter — you add it in your backend metadata or sidecar file. Registry-side scoping is fully BYO.

Per-call runtime scoping via SkillPaths in ai.WithUse(&middleware.Skills{SkillPaths: [global, tenants/<id>]}). Different requests can attach middleware with different paths. No publish-time scoping — everything registered with genkit.DefineTool/DefinePrompt is global to that *genkit.Genkit instance.

BYO via BaseStore namespace tuples (e.g. ('skills','global',...) vs ('skills', tenant_id, ...)), convention only; on the paid server, @auth.on.store / @auth.on.assistants handlers can filter what each caller sees. A 3.1.1 store fix stops Postgres/SQLite namespace-prefix matching from leaking across tenants with shared id prefixes. No first-class scope or visibility primitive in OSS.
No registry-side or runtime scoping primitive. You write your own loader feeding tool_retriever or tools=[...].

Registry side: stored agents/skills have authorId and visibility ('private'|'public'), favorites, and organizationId/projectId on scorers/datasets/experiments; no tenantId on skills. Runtime: SkillsResolver and other dynamic resolvers read requestContext, and RBAC + FGA (ee/) gate stored entities over HTTP. The two halves are not wired together, so a resolver must still filter by author.

Runtime-only scoping, now friendlier: every source receives SkillsSourceContext(agent, session), so a FilteringSkillsSource predicate can read session state, and CachingSkillsSource accepts a cache_isolation_key_selector for per-tenant caches (no per-tenant SkillsProvider needed any more). No publish-time scope: tenancy is encoded in skill metadata and enforced by your predicate. Stays at 2, level with ADK Go's ctx-aware BYO wrapper.
Per-agent, per-instance at construction time (or agent.clone(tools=[...])). No dynamic per-turn filtering of skills like there is for tools (is_enabled callable). No publish-time scoping.

Different defaultManifest per SandboxAgent or options.sandbox.manifestPatch override at run time. No built-in tenant-aware skill catalog and no registry-side scoping; you compose a manifest yourself based on runContext.context.tenantId.

Runtime: dynamic capability factories resolve per run from ctx.deps, so a per-tenant Skills/SubAgents/toolset can be built each run; ManagedPrompt(targeting_key=..., attributes=...) gives deterministic per-user/tenant prompt variants (harness 0.x). No publish-time scoping for skills, and include/exclude is explicitly not an access-control boundary.
No registry-side or runtime scoping primitive.

Per AgentSkills instance: one plugin per tenant, or mutate plugin.set_available_skills([...]) between invocations (affects all agents sharing the plugin instance). No publish-time scoping; all filtering is runtime.

Per-Agent: AgentSkills attaches to one agent and all invocations on that agent see the same catalog. Per-tenant requires creating one AgentSkills instance per tenant. Skill.allowedTools is parsed but explicitly not yet enforced (experimental).
BYO. You track skillId-tenant mapping in your DB and conditionally pass providerOptions.anthropic.skills per runtimeContext.tenantId.

No draft/active/deprecated/retired lifecycle states. Skills are either in the filesystem the Source reads or not. Multi-environment promotion is done via separate git branches or buckets per env — entirely operational.

Components subsystem only: create writes a DRAFT, publish_component / set-current promotes it, with archive/restore, via /components REST or StudioTools. No separate multi-environment promotion or approval gate (use separate AgentOS deployments per environment) and skills are not covered.
No publish/promote/retire workflow.
No publishing workflow. Multi-environment story is operational (separate git branches, separate buckets per env).
No draft -> review -> publish -> promote pipeline. You build it yourself with a Git repo per tenant for .claude/ trees, CI that publishes to per-tenant S3 buckets, and a sync agent on each pod.

Skills: crewai create skill -> crewai skill publish [--org] (checks git state) -> crewai skill install/reference; no draft -> review -> promote stages, no environments and no approval gates in OSS. Agents/deployments go through the AMP dashboard and crewai deploy create|push|status|logs|remove, with multi-environment via separate deployments. Kept at 2 as in May; the refreshed report no longer documents a draft -> published state for Agent Repositories.
No draft/review/promote/multi-environment workflow. Build with git tags and your own CI.
No draft/active/deprecated states, no review/approval gates, no promotion across environments. Skills are source code shipped with your binary.

OSS has no publishing workflow. For whole graphs, langgraph deploy pushes to LangSmith Deployment (paid), which is a code deployment pipeline, not a draft -> review -> publish workflow for skills. The Assistants API is paid hosted only.

No draft/review/promote workflow. LlamaHub was a community directory of packs and its links have been retired from the docs; llamactl (separate repo) deploys whole agent apps, not individual resources.

Stored agents, skills, prompt blocks, scorers and MCP clients have status draft -> published -> archived with an activeVersionId, driven by the Studio editor, and callers can pin 'draft' or 'published' per request for previews. No multi-environment promotion (dev -> staging -> prod) or approval gate between environments; app-level mastra deploy handles environments. Raised from 1 (correction: the lifecycle already existed at the May commit but was reported as absent), level with Agno's component draft -> publish flow.
There is no draft -> active -> retired model. No publishing workflow shipped.
No publishing workflow.
No draft/review/publish/promote stages, no multi-environment story.

No promotion workflow for skills/agents (PyPI packaging by convention). For prompts only, Logfire ManagedPrompt labels and percentage rollouts give a draft-to-production path outside the codebase (harness 0.x). No staged environments or approval gates. Raised from 0 for the prompt-only primitive.
No publishing workflow.

No draft -> review -> publish -> promote pipeline; Git plus CI is the de facto control plane. The CLI /export writes a runnable project with bundled skills and policies, which helps packaging but is not a promotion workflow.
No publishing workflow.
No draft/review/publish/promote, no multi-environment, no approval gates.

No lifecycle states, RBAC or approval workflow for skills; operational tooling only. Agent Registry entries are governed by the Google Cloud service (IAM), outside ADK. authn/authz in the REST server are user-level, not resource-level.

No lifecycle states (draft, active, deprecated, retired), no RBAC at the resource layer.

No lifecycle, no RBAC.

No RBAC, no lifecycle states.

row: Built-in tools (web search, file ops, exec)

Most modules are still thin SDK wrappers. No anchor-matched Edit and no Monitor-style streaming process, so depth is below Claude Code's toolkit; breadth is among the widest in the survey.

row: Built-in tools (web search, file ops, exec)

Tools are thin stdlib wrappers; the sandbox layer is the differentiator, not tool depth.

Tools encode the best practices the benchmark cares about: line-numbered Read, anchor-matched Edit, sandboxed Bash, Monitor that streams stdout. Highest-depth catalog in the survey, tied with the TS SDK.

row: Built-in tools (web search, file ops, exec)
details: The catalog (ToolInputSchemas, 0.3.286) covers Bash (run_in_background, timeout), Read (line numbers, offset/limit, PDF pages), Write, anchor-based Edit with uniqueness validation, Glob, ripgrep Grep, WebFetch/WebSearch, Agent (worktree/remote isolation), Workflow, Monitor (line-event streaming), task/cron tools, NotebookEdit, Skill, AskUserQuestion and MCP resource tools. Same battle-tested toolset as Claude Code and still the strongest built-in surface in the comparison; servers should pass an explicit tools list to switch off product-facing tools.

row: Built-in tools (web search, file ops, exec)
details: About 82 packages in crewai-tools: web search (Serper/SerpAPI/Tavily/Brave/Exa), heavy scraping (Firecrawl, Scrapfly, Brightdata, Stagehand, Apify), file/document/vector backends, E2B and Daytona sandbox tools, vision, GitHub/arxiv, AMP/Composio/Zapier bridges. Depth is shallow: no bash in OSS (allow_code_execution deprecated), no anchor-matched Edit, no line-numbered Read, no Monitor. Breadth is excellent but agent-aware patterns are thin.

row: Built-in tools (web search, file ops, exec)
details: Core eino ships no standalone tools, but the filesystem middleware bundles ls/read_file/write_file/edit_file/glob/grep/execute with line-numbered reads, exact-string edits and an oversize-result stash; read_file now also reads images and PDFs (multimodal backends). Other middleware adds skill, tool_search, todos and plan tasks. eino-ext adds MCP clients, DuckDuckGo/Google/Bing/SearxNG/Wikipedia/HTTP, commandline, browser automation, and provider-hosted server tools via the agentic adapters. Broad by name, shallower per tool than Claude's catalog (no Monitor, no multi-anchor edit). Held at 3: the refresh additions are incremental and the May baseline was already crediting the filesystem middleware.

New experimental middleware adds delegate_to_<agent>, background-task control tools and read/write_artifact. No first-party web search, bash, fetch, glob, grep or monitor; code execution and Google Search are provider features of googlegenai. The FS tools are well engineered but the catalog stays small.

row: Built-in tools (web search, file ops, exec)

row: Built-in tools (web search, file ops, exec)
details: Hosted tools (webSearch, fileSearch, codeInterpreter, imageGeneration, hostedMcp, toolSearch, programmaticToolCalling) are thin descriptors executed at OpenAI. Locally executed surface is richer than May's scoring credited: shellTool (local/container), applyPatchTool and computerTool via executor interfaces, plus sandbox-agent tools exec_command/write_stdin (PTY with output budgets), apply_patch/view_image (stacked-anchor handling) and load_skill, and an experimental Codex tool. The first-party pydantic-ai-harness (0.x, now in the monorepo) adds agent-aware tools: FileSystem with line-numbered paged read, content-hash optimistic writes, batched exact-match edit, regex search and glob; Shell with background command control and allow/deny lists; Coder, Planning, CodeMode, Playwright/BrowserUse and many integrations. details: Two sources now. The SDK vends shell and file_editor (both routed through the agent Sandbox; file_editor does view-range/create/str_replace/insert), http_request, web_fetch (markdown or agentic mode), notebook, sleep, handoff_to_user, mcp_router and a2a_client; the harness adds read/write/edit, web_search, programmatic_tool_caller and subagent.
