The UI is hosted rather than bundled, but the local server plus REPL is first-class (report 20.1).

No first-party playground. Run via `cargo run --example <name>` against the 20+ examples directory. A separate `AutoAgents-CLI` repo provides a YAML-driven HTTP runner but is out of scope for the SDK itself.
The `claude` CLI binary is itself a TUI you can run locally. The Python SDK ships `examples/quick_start.py` for headless runs but there is no separate dev UI for the SDK consumer.

The bundled `claude` binary is the interactive Claude Code CLI, a full local runner for the same skills, agents, settings-defined hooks and MCP config. SDK code runs as a plain script under `bun` or `node --import tsx`; there is no SDK-level playground or web dev UI. Scored the same as the Python SDK, which exposes the identical CLI runner, so the previous 3 vs 4 split was calibration noise (report 20.1).

`crewai run` now opens a full-screen Textual TUI (tasks/agents/tokens sidebar, plan checklist, activity timeline, streaming output) and also runs declarative flows. `crewai chat` is a terminal chat and conversational Flows get a conversational TUI; `crewai create` scaffolds crews, flows and skills, and `crewai flow plot` renders the graph. No first-party web playground in OSS; AMP Studio is the hosted builder. Stays at 4 because of the missing web UI (report 20.1).

No `eino dev` CLI, TUI or playground. CloudWeGo ships IntelliJ-targeted orchestration and visual debug plugins, the v0.9 `ChatWithEino` quickstart gives a console app plus a local web page, and `eino-ext/acp` exposes an agent to ACP editors. These are examples and IDE plugins rather than a first-party runner, so it stays at 1 (report 20.1).

`genkit start -- go run .` sets `GENKIT_ENV=dev` and starts the reflection server behind the Dev UI: action runner (flows, tools, prompts, agents via bidi actions), trace viewer with realtime spans and per-span logs, prompt playground, middleware config forms, background-task panel, datasets and evals. Samples also ship interactive CLIs (`basic-agents/cli.go`). First-class local sandbox (report 20.1).

`langgraph dev` runs the ELv2 `langgraph-api` dev server (needs `langgraph-cli[inmem]` and Python 3.11+) with in-memory persistence, hot reload and the LangGraph Studio web UI to visualise the graph, step state, send messages and trigger interrupts. It can now serve over HTTPS (`--certfile`). Studio is closed-source and tied to LangSmith, but the dev workflow is first-class (report 20.1).

Core still has no agent CLI or playground; `llama-index-cli` is for indexing. The refreshed report notes the vendor's separate `llamactl serve` runs workflow apps locally and `llama-agents-server` mounts a debugger UI at `/`. These live in another repo and were not analysed at code level, so this is only a small first-party primitive (report 20.1).

`mastra dev` boots a local server plus Mastra Studio (`packages/playground`): run agents, inspect traces, run evals and experiments, edit stored agents and skills, view memory. File-based routing auto-discovers agents, workflows, storage and observability config. `mastracode/` (TUI, web, SDK) offers a terminal loop, and `createCodingAgent` exposes its defaults. First-class (report 20.1).

`agent-framework-devui` (`devui ./agents --port 8080`; .NET `Microsoft.Agents.AI.DevUI` and an Aspire hosting package) auto-discovers agents and workflows and serves an OpenAI-compatible API plus a debug web UI. It is labelled beta and a sample app, not for production, which caps it at 4. Harness console samples in Python and .NET add a TUI (report 20.1).

`run_demo_loop` (`src/agents/repl.py`) is a streaming terminal REPL that surfaces tool calls. `UnixLocalSandboxClient` and `DockerSandboxClient` run Sandbox Agents locally and `agents.testing` runs workflows offline, but those are workspace and test tooling, not a dev runner. No web playground or TUI (report 20.1).

No CLI or playground; agent code runs under `tsx`, `node`, `deno` or `bun`. `examples/sandbox/basic.ts` with `UnixLocalSandboxClient` or Docker is the closest thing to a local workspace runner. Unlike the Python SDK there is no REPL helper (report 20.1).

`clai` (`uvx clai`, `-a module:agent`, `clai web`), `agent.to_web()` (Starlette plus prebuilt chat UI with model/tool pickers and tool-approval UI) and `to_cli()` cover terminal and browser use. New in the 0.x Harness satellite: `pydantic-clai2`, a coding TUI with session persistence; ACP support for editors is experimental. Kept at 4 because there is no trace or graph view in the local UI (report 20.1).

`cli_chatbot` (`crates/rig-agent/src/integrations/cli_chatbot.rs`) wraps an agent in a stdin/stdout loop, and 70 runnable example packages (`cargo run -p <name>`) cover most features. `rig-candle` runs small models locally on CPU, including a WASM browser chat example. No TUI, web dev UI or playground (report 20.1).

The new first-party `strands` CLI (`@strands-agents/cli`, `strands-cli/`) offers an Ink TUI, readline mode, `--print` one-shot and an ACP server, with slash commands (`/tools`, `/export`, skills). It runs the TypeScript harness by default and can launch a Python project with `strands --agent ./agent.py`, so a Python user needs Node. It is a 0.1.x package with no web UI and the older agent-builder is archived, so 3 (report 20.1).

The new `strands-cli` (`@strands-agents/cli`, 0.1.4) is an Ink terminal chat on `@strands-agents/harness` with `--print`, `--acp-server`, `--session` resume, `--skills`, `--mcp-config`, `--agent <path>` (agent.ts, agent.py, folder or ZIP) and `/export`. `strandly` no longer exists. The package is days old, its UX changed daily in September, and there is no web UI or trace view, so 3 rather than 4 (report 20.1).

New `@ai-sdk/tui` `runAgentTUI({ agent })` runs a local `ToolLoopAgent` or `HarnessAgent` in an interactive terminal with streaming markdown, tool cards and approval prompts, or attaches to a remote endpoint. `@ai-sdk/devtools` adds a local web viewer. There is still no web chat playground like Mastra Studio, and the usual pattern is a Next.js example, so 3 (report 20.1).

`DebugTelemetry` buffers recent spans and logs in memory and serves `/debug/trace/{event_id}` and `/debug/trace/session/{session_id}` plus agent-graph routes; the Web UI uses them to show past runs. Since v2.5 these routes sit behind opt-in `-include_debug_api` and the handler warns against enabling them in production. Production tracing exports OTel to Datadog, Cloud Trace or Jaeger (report 20.2).

Traces appear in the AgentOS UI (hosted, with latency and error stats) or can be queried from the `agno_traces` and `agno_spans` tables. `AgentOSTools` can report usage, latency and failures conversationally. No local trace viewer ships in the OSS package (report 20.2).
Indirect — push traces to an OTLP collector (Tempo/Jaeger/Datadog) via `autoagents-telemetry` and inspect there. No first-party viewer.
Local JSONL transcripts at `~/.claude/projects/...`. CLI ships `/context`, `/cost`, `/status` commands and SDK exposes `get_context_usage()` programmatically. No GUI replay tool.

Local JSONL at `~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<sessionId>.jsonl` (inspect with `jq` or `claude --resume`); with OTel enabled any trace UI works. `/context` results carry a structured `context_usage` payload. No GUI replay tool (report 20.2).

Local: the run TUI, checkpoint and memory TUIs, and rich console output with `verbose=True`. External: 17 documented observability integrations. AMP offers a traces dashboard (the CLI prints a link after traces finalise). No local trace viewer or replay UI (report 20.2).
No local built-in trace viewer. Remote integration with Langfuse/LangSmith/APMPlus/CozeLoop dashboards is the supported path.

note: Dev UI trace viewer + reflection API
details: The Dev UI timeline trace viewer covers generate iterations, tool calls and middleware, with per-span logs. Realtime `span_start`/`span_end` events stream over SSE so in-progress agent runs are visible, and traces are queryable via the reflection API. First-class local inspection (report 20.2).
LangGraph Studio (closed-source, part of LangSmith) visualises runs when `langgraph dev` is running; LangSmith (paid cloud) covers production traces. No OSS local viewer, hence 3 (report 20.2).
Via OTel exporter into your tracing backend (Phoenix, Jaeger, Langfuse, etc.). No local TUI viewer.
Mastra Studio has a built-in trace inspector and spans+metrics from `observability/` are queryable. Langfuse and OTel exporters are available for offboarding.

DevUI shows traces via `--instrumentation` and a trace viewer panel, and DevUI renders Aspire traces since 1.19.0. DevUI is beta and a sample app, so the score stays at 4. OTel instrumentation is on by default in the core (report 20.2, 12).
Via the OpenAI Traces dashboard (free, hosted) or any of the 25+ partner exporters. No local OSS viewer ships.
Default exporter goes to platform.openai.com/traces (hosted only). Local inspection requires the `ConsoleSpanExporter` or wiring your own.
Logfire UI (hosted) is the primary trace inspector; any OTel backend (Jaeger/Tempo/Honeycomb) for self-hosted use. No local-only built-in UI.

New `rig-cassette` records effect logs via `AgentBuilder::record_to` and replays them with identity checks, plus provider HTTP cassettes for deterministic replay. Logs are serialisable JSON you can inspect, but there is no viewer; the live path is `tracing-subscriber` and OTel (`examples/otel`). Replay primitive on top of an otherwise OTel-only story, so 2 (report 20.2, 19.4).
OTel exporter into your viewer of choice. No built-in trace inspection surface.
`AgentResult.traces` exposes a tree of spans in-process — programmatic only, no GUI. Pipe to OTel and use any OTel-compatible viewer (Jaeger, Tempo, Honeycomb, Phoenix) for replay.

`@ai-sdk/devtools` captures runs and steps through telemetry and serves a local web UI (`npx @ai-sdk/devtools`, port 4983) for inspecting past runs; `@ai-sdk/otel` ships traces to Jaeger, Tempo or Honeycomb. It is local-development only and does not re-execute runs, which matches the ADK Go and DevUI cases scored 4. The May report missed devtools (report 19.4, 20.2).
Not provided. The Web UI picks app and user, so simulating a tenant means another `appName`/`userId`, or headers when a header-based `Authenticator` is configured (report 20.3).

Not a tenant picker, but with `user_isolation=True` switching the JWT, PAT or `NoAuthIdentityMiddleware` user id switches the visible sessions, memories and knowledge, and an `AgentFactory` builds per-request agents from verified claims. Same level as LangGraph's per-run context plus local `@auth` handlers, so 2 (report 20.3, 6).
Not provided — bring your own tenant scoping in caller code.
BYO: different `cwd` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` per tenant. No first-party tenant switcher (report 20.3).
Change `cwd`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `settings`/`managedSettings` and `env` per `query()`. No tenant switcher UI (report 20.3).

note: `crewai org switch` is AMP auth only
details: `crewai org list|switch|current` switches AMP organizations, which only changes which org's Agent/Skills Repository refs resolve. It is not a local tenant-context switch because OSS has no tenant primitive. The closest local equivalent is a conversational Flow with a tenant-prefixed `session_id` and your own ContextVar (report 20.3).
Not provided — there is no local sandbox to switch tenant context in.

note: no tenant concept in Dev UI
details: Not provided. The Dev UI has no concept of tenant; you manually pass tenant headers in the action-runner form.
Studio UI does not directly model tenant switching, but you pass `context: {"tenant_id": ...}` in the run-create payload, so testing tenant-scoped behaviour is a single form field.
Not provided — caller-side tenant scoping only.

Studio supports per-tab request-context overrides and per-tab model overrides (1.52.0) and auth-provider sessions for testing RBAC. There is no dedicated tenant picker beyond editing request context, but it is still the strongest first-party UI for this in the cohort. The refreshed report no longer cites the RBAC impersonation flow, so kept at 4 only on the per-tab override UI (report 20.3).

Not built in as a tenant switcher, but DevUI forwards `extra_body.function_invocation_kwargs` to `agent.run()` since 1.15.0, so a tester can set `tenant_id` per request. That is the same mechanism class as LangGraph's `context` field (2), though the values are client-supplied and untrusted. No tenant picker or role switching, and DevUI is beta (report 20.3, 8).
N/A at SDK level — you switch by changing the `context=...` passed to `Runner.run`. No tenant primitive.
Not provided as a built-in. You toggle via your own env vars/context.

Not built into `clai` or the web UI. `create_api_app(deps=...)` fixes one deps object for all requests, so tenants are switched by launching a different agent module or deps (`clai --agent tenant_acme:agent`). The web UI switches models, not tenants (report 20.3).
Not provided. No tenant or org switching primitive in the SDK or any local tooling.
Not provided — no tenant primitive in the SDK.
Not provided. The CLI has sessions and a saved profile, not tenant contexts; to test tenant-scoped behaviour you pass a different `invocationState` yourself (report 20.3).
BYO. You write the dev UI and switch `runtimeContext` in your own form.
No first-party hot reload. Skills are read at toolset construction or preload and agents are Go code, so changes need a restart or an external watcher such as `air` (report 20.4).
`agent_os.serve(reload=True)` enables uvicorn auto-reload on `.py` and `.yaml` changes (`os/app.py:1518-1521`). Process-level reload rather than in-flight skill swap, but first-class flag.
Not provided. Rust compilation means change-skill = recompile; tools like `cargo watch` are external.

Skills, agents and plugins load on every subprocess spawn, so editing a SKILL.md takes effect on the next `query()` with no cache to flush. Exception: system-prompt edits on a resumed session are ignored because of the first-request snapshot; set `snapshot: False` while iterating on prompt text (report 20.4).

New `Query.reloadSkills()` and `SessionStart` `reloadSkills: true` let skills change without restarting the session, alongside `reloadPlugins()`, `reloadOutputStyles()`, `applyFlagSettings()` and `setMcpServers()`. Gaps: no default file watcher (wire `FileChanged` + `watchPaths` yourself), sub-agent definitions in `Options.agents` need a new query, and a prompt change lands at the next compaction (report 20.4).

No watch mode: nothing in `lib/cli` uses `watchfiles` or `--reload`. Changing a SKILL.md, YAML/JSON definition or Python code needs a new run, and long-lived processes must rebuild the agent (report 20.4).

The filesystem skill `Backend` re-reads SKILL.md on every `List`/`Get`, and `agentsmd` re-reads AGENTS.md on every model call, so skill and prompt edits apply without restart. Go code still needs `air` or `reflex` (report 20.4).

SKILL.md is re-scanned on every `Generate` call by the Skills middleware so changes are picked up live. `.prompt` files are loaded only at `genkit.Init` — restart required unless you call `LoadPromptDir` again. Go code uses `air`/`wgo`.
`langgraph dev` reloads the graph on file save by default (`--no-reload` disables it). Skill and prompt iteration is BYO because skills are not first-class (report 20.4).

Not provided in this repo; Python reload is `importlib.reload` or `jurigged`. The external `llamactl` is said to support local development with hot reload, but that repo was not analysed (report 20.4).

`mastra dev` watches sources and reloads agents, tools and workflows. Workspace skills refresh in the background (up to 30 s stale) and stored skills or agents edited in Studio apply on the next request, with draft vs published selectable. Most polished story in the cohort (report 20.4).

`devui ./agents --reload` watches sources and `POST /v1/entities/{entity_id}/reload` reloads one entity. Skill caching can be disabled (`disable_caching=True`) or given a short `cache_refresh_interval`. Reload lives in DevUI, which is labelled beta, so the maturity cap applies and the previous 5 is lowered to 4 (report 20.4, 10).

note: new agent picks up SKILL.md edits
details: Library with no watcher or reload flag; reload semantics depend on your host (`uvicorn --reload`). The refreshed report notes lazy skills are re-listed per `Skills` instance, so creating a new agent per request picks up edited SKILL.md files without a restart. That is a small primitive, comparable to the host-level options scored 1 elsewhere (report 20.4).
Not provided. Use `tsx watch` or `nodemon` yourself.

Skills and disk sub-agents are re-read from the workspace on every run, so a SKILL.md edit applies on the next run without restart, and `ManagedPrompt` picks up new Logfire prompt versions per run. Code and static prompts still need `uvicorn --reload` for `to_web()`. Same shape as Genkit Go (skills live, code needs restart), so 3 (report 20.4).
Not provided; recompile. Runtime changes are limited to `ToolServerHandle` tool add/remove and `agent.set_model` (report 20.4).

Tools hot-reload from `./tools/` via `Agent(load_tools_from_directory=True)` and a `watchdog`-based `ToolWatcher`. Skills load once per agent on first invocation, `set_available_skills` resets them, and there is no watcher. The new CLI re-reads an imported project on each launch and rebuilds the profile after in-CLI edits (report 20.4).

No file watcher. Programmatic reloads work: `AgentSkills.setAvailableSkills(...)`, `toolRegistry.add/remove`, mutable `systemPrompt` and `model`, and `agent.tool.X.invoke()` to exercise a tool without a model call. Cedar can re-read policy files via `CedarAuthorization.reload()`, and the CLI can edit and reload a TypeScript-defined agent (report 20.4).

note: host HMR only, no skill primitive
details: Whatever the host gives you (Next.js HMR, `tsx watch`). Harness skills can be swapped between turns via `prepareCall` without recreating the session, but no file watcher ships and skills do not exist on `ToolLoopAgent` (report 20.4).
